newsitem.title: USA: Callon sees natgas production increase.
newsitem.headline: Callon sees natgas production increase.

text.p: Callon Petroleum Co said Friday production is expected to begin within 30 days from its first two wells drilled in federal waters offshore Louisiana.

At Main Pass Block 163, the company said, its No. A-1 well encountered 54 feet of net pay in a new reservoir discovery at a true vertical subsea depth of approximately 3,300 feet. It was drilled from a surface location adjacent to the company's production facility at Block 163. Callon owns a 100 percent working interest the No. A-1 well and production facilities.

At Chandeleur Block 40, the company said its No. A-3 well encountered 44 feet of net pay at a true vertical subsea depth of some 3,855 feet. It was drilled from a surface location at the company's production facility at Block 40, where Callon has a 52 percent working interest.
The company also said it is drilling at Main Pass 161, in which it owns a 100 percent working interest.

As a result of these two wells, coupled with the replacement of compression equipment at the Chandeleur Block 40 and Main Pass Block 163 production facilities, Callon said, it anticipates a substantial increase in its natural gas production rates by year-end.
